newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: THINLY-TRADED SOLCHEM SURGES ON UNIT SELL.
newsitem.headline: THINLY-TRADED SOLCHEM SURGES ON UNIT SELL.

text.p: Tightly-traded packaging and printing firm Solchem Investment Holdings Ltd surged more than 92 percent on Thursday after earlier agreeing to sell one of its units in a move which could make it a cash shell, dealers said.
The share lurched to 250 cents in early trade -- its richest level ever since it was fist listed in 1987.
But by 0935 GMT it had retreated slightly to 230 cents with 108,300 shares having changed hands.
It was the biggest gainer by percentage on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE).
"It's quite obviously on the announcement but you have to remember that this a fairly tightly traded stock and so any jump is exaggerated," one JSE dealer said.

He declined to expand on what the deal meant for Solchem other than what the company itself had said -- that it would either become a cash shell with nine months to acquire new assets or be delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
At the moment Solchem's share price was looking a little inflated and could come back a little further on the day, dealers added.
"I think it's overshot the market somewhat and could come back a little bit later. It will probably find a comfortable trading range between 180 and 200 cents," one dealer said.
Solchem said on Thursday that it had sealed a deal for CTP Holdings Ltd to buy its Solchem (PTY) Ltd unit for 54.2 million rand at 130 cents a share. CTP owns 79.8 percent of Solchem.
CTP was last steady at 51.25 rand with a meagre 500 shares trading in two moves.
The deal will also see Plascon buy Solchem (Pty)'s liquid and sheet-fed printing inks operations for 25.6 million rand while Solchem (Pty) will buy Plascon's web ink operations for 3.1 million rand.
